A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAM failure-mode study. All 24 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, figures, and the new table, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MNIST training experiments, repeated-seed radius sweeps, stochastic ResNet-18/CIFAR-100 experiments, and synthetic visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds full-batch ResNet-18 experiments on CIFAR-10/100, reported in Table 1 and Figures 8–9.

M1.justification: The normalized SAM perturbation, shifted-gradient update, and initial 10% GD/SGD phase followed by SAM are unchanged. Calling the switching strategy a warm-start and revising the mathematical definition of hallucinated minimizers do not change the training procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds CIFAR-10 image classification while retaining MNIST, CIFAR-100, and the synthetic example. Full-batch evaluation on the already included CIFAR-100 changes the protocol rather than adding another task or domain.

E2.justification: The method comparison remains SAM-only versus the same GD/SGD-to-SAM switching schedule. The new CIFAR experiments sweep standard SAM's radius, including zero; cited SAM variants are not added as evaluated competitors.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a separate full-batch CIFAR protocol with ResNet-18, 10,000 steps, learning rate 0.001, no augmentation, and radii from 0 to 2 in increments of 0.5. It also introduces GradRatio and LossGap diagnostics and reports original versus shifted losses and gradients. The earlier MNIST and stochastic CIFAR protocols remain intact.

E4.justification: Table 1 and Appendix C.2 add a substantial mechanism analysis testing whether shifted/unshifted mismatch persists in larger ReLU networks under deterministic training. Final-gradient measurements and paired loss trajectories across radii extend the evidence beyond the earlier small smooth-network example. Existing perturb-and-return, switching, and synthetic sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 clarifies that thin trajectory curves represent individual seeds and bold curves represent means. For the stochastic trajectories, this corrects v1 Appendix C.2's description of standard-deviation shading; the actual panels are unchanged. Existing counts of 80, 5, and 16 seeds and the other mean/standard-deviation summaries remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds full-batch CIFAR loss and gradient results absent from v1. For example, Table 1 reports CIFAR-10 at radius 1.5 with original/shifted losses of 0.773/0.001 and gradient norms of 11.932/0.011. These are new-setting findings, not improvements over matched v1 results. Retained stochastic peak accuracies remain 77.05% for SAM-only and 77.49% for switching.

T1.justification: Definition 2.1 adds shifted-gradient stationarity as an explicit requirement. Both existence theorems now establish nontrivial radius intervals, supported by new Lemmas A.5 and A.10. The manifold theorem is recast under C2 regularity and explicit local preimage assumptions. v2 also corrects the Jacobian transpose, multiplier signs, and surrogate smoothness constant, adds a Hessian-norm sufficient stability condition, and revises the neural-network analyticity assumptions.

C1.justification: The introduction strengthens existence from some radius to an interval and centers the contribution on stationary shifted-gradient dynamics despite a nonzero original gradient. It also narrows the empirical claims to evidence consistent with the mechanism and recasts switching from a proposed remedy into an established warm-start safeguard that mitigates the failure mode.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1's broad claim that most modern networks are real-analytic with conditional statements about suitable deterministic networks. It explicitly treats loss slices as suggestive rather than certification and stochastic/ReLU observations as outside the formal guarantees. Section 3.1 also adds an acute-angle interpretation explaining the stability condition.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 documents gradient accumulation across the training set, normalization, absent augmentation, and optimizer settings for the new full-batch CIFAR experiments. v2 additionally states that the 10% warm-start fraction was not tuned. Existing implementation details and the same repository access information are retained; the repository disclosure is relocated.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 substantially refocuses positioning on large-radius, discrete-time SAM and prior switching schedules. v2 specifically attributes warm-start precedents to Andriushchenko and Flammarion (2022) and disclaims proposing a new training recipe. It also removes substantial portions of the broader applications and flat-minima literature survey while retaining the central SAM theory references.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, theoretical explanations, experiments, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The dynamical and manifold subsections and their proofs exchange order, the analyticity appendix moves, and references move after the appendices. These changes substantially reorganize retained content as well as accommodating additions.

P2.justification: v2 changes typography, headings, text width, and figure sizing and placement throughout. It removes v1 Figure 3's maximizer-set illustration, adds Table 1 and two CIFAR trajectory figures, and separates the final synthetic figure collections across pages. Most retained plot panels are unchanged, although captions and numbering are revised.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses central weaknesses by explicitly connecting the definition to SAM-update stationarity, correcting derivative and convergence-proof details, and supporting interval-of-radius existence with additional arguments. New deterministic CIFAR diagnostics strengthen the mechanistic evidence. More careful treatment of loss slices, analyticity, stochastic observations, and warm-start novelty improves the match between evidence and claims. Stochastic and nonsmooth convergence guarantees remain open, but the revisions substantially improve correctness and evidential support.
